capabilities: Map a folder of Markdown prompt files to command palette entries
Stream LLM responses into the editor selection or cursor
Configure per-prompt behavior with frontmatter (info-mode popup, selection-only, context size)
Run ad-hoc one-off prompts through a built-in custom prompt command
Manage multiple OpenAI-compatible provider and model presets with capability checks
extras: The author notes results depend heavily on the user's prompting skill, and the demo used OpenRouter's google/gemini-3-flash-preview model.
motivation: The author built it because repeatedly reusing prompts such as 'improve writing', 'translate', or 'make this a bullet-list' by copy-pasting gets tedious quickly.
problem: Reusing common prompts like translate or improve writing requires copy-pasting text into an external chat tool, which is tedious inside Obsidian.

relations.evidence: Use your own OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenAI, OpenRouter, and others with compatible endpoints)
I used OpenRouter's google/gemini-3-flash-preview for demo

summary: Turns Markdown prompt files in a vault folder into Obsidian commands that run the prompt against the active note via any OpenAI-compatible LLM provider.
